attributes.body:
そうだ is one of the 18 primary auxiliary verbs in Japanese, and can be used in two (2) different ways. The broad meaning in each of its applications is that something 'seems' to be a certain way. Due to this, そう is regularly translated as 'seems like', 'looks like', or 'appears as though'.

In this lesson, we will focus on the form that is used with the conjunctive (stem) form of words. Please examine the structure guide to see these forms.

Caution

そう may also be used when attached to the い-Adjective, ない. In this case, there is a unique conjugation rule which we will need to be careful of. As always, い will be removed from ない before attaching そう. However, さ will be inserted between な, and そう. This creates the expression なさそう.

Note that this addition of さ does not happen with verbs. This is due to the ない that is used with negative verbs being an auxiliary verb, and not an い-Adjective. With the auxiliary verb ない, simply remove the い, before adding そう directly to the stem.

Caution

This そう is utilized exclusively to make predictions/guesses about something based on visual information. It is relatively low confidence, so should not be used for things that are obvious. In these cases, みたい would be used instead.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar
[AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.body: The main difference between そう and らしい① lies in the source of information. そう implies speculation based on personal observation, e.g. 面白そう ('It looks interesting.'). らしい is based on secondhand information or inference, e.g. 面白いらしい ('I hear it's interesting.' or 'Apparently, it's interesting.').

first_relatable.title: そう
first_relatable.meaning: Look like, Appear, Seem, Have a feeling that

attributes.body: ような気がする and そう both express impressions, but with different nuance. ような気がする conveys personal intuition or vague feeling, i.e. something you sense even without clear reason. On the other hand, そう is typically based on observable clues or appearance. In that sense, ような気がする is more subjective and less confident than そう.

second_relatable.title: そう
second_relatable.meaning: Look like, Appear, Seem, Have a feeling that

attributes.body: Both っぽい and そう express appearance or impression, but differ in nuance and usage. そう attaches to word stems and is neutral and often based on observation, e.g. 雨が降りそう ('It looks like it'll rain.'). っぽい is casual and attaches to nouns to mean '~ish' or '~like', e.g. 子供っぽい 'childish'. Unlike そう, it often carries a negative or demeaning tone.

attributes.body: のように・のような and そう both express impressions, but with different nuance. のように・のような show direct comparison, like 'like' or 'as if,' e.g. 春のように暖かい ('It's warm like spring.'). そう expresses a perceived impression based on observation, e.g. 暖かそう ('It seems warm.').

second_relatable.title: そう
second_relatable.meaning: Look like, Appear, Seem, Have a feeling that

attributes.body: Both みたい and そう can mean 'seems like', but differ in nuance and usage. みたい compares something to another, e.g. 春みたい ('It's like spring.') or is based on reliable evidence, e.g. 面白いみたい ('Apparently it's interesting.' i.e. based on something you've heard). そう is based on appearance or sensory impression, e.g. 面白そう ('It looks/sounds interesting.').

second_relatable.title: そう
second_relatable.meaning: Look like, Appear, Seem, Have a feeling that

attributes.body: ように・ような and そう both convey impressions, but with different nuance. ように・ような expresses direct comparison or similarity, like 'as if' or 'like,' e.g. 春が来たように暖かい ('It's warm as if spring had come.'). そう is based on the speaker's observation or feeling, e.g. 暖かそう ('It seems warm.').

second_relatable.title: そう
second_relatable.meaning: Look like, Appear, Seem, Have a feeling that

attributes.body: そう is used to express that something seems likely based on perception or indirect signs, e.g. 雨が降りそう ('It looks like it's going to rain.'). In contrast, そうもない (or そうにない) indicates that there are no signs of something happening, e.g. 雨が降りそうもない ('It doesn't seem like it'll rain at all.').

first_relatable.meaning: Very unlikely to, Does not seem that, Does not appear that

second_relatable.title: そう
second_relatable.meaning: Look like, Appear, Seem, Have a feeling that

attributes.body: The たい form expresses personal desires, such as 日本に行きたい ('I want to go to Japan'), though, the たい form is typically not used for expressing others' desires. One way that we can comment on another person's desires, however, is to use the そう form, meaning 'appears to.' For example 日本に行きたそう can be used to mean 'They seem to want to go to Japan.'

second_relatable.title: そう
second_relatable.meaning: Look like, Appear, Seem, Have a feeling that

attributes.body: にみえる and そう both express that something 'seems' a certain way, but with different nuance. にみえる specifically refers to visual appearance and can be combined with そう, e.g. 面白そうにみえる ('It looks interesting.'). そう alone expresses general impression and doesn't necessarily rely on visual cues, e.g. 面白そう ('It seems interesting.'), which could be based on hearing about it, etc.

first_relatable.meaning: To look, To seem, To appear
